The test image shows a tomato plant laid out with:
- Extensive pale/bleached elongated lesions on the main stems
- Whole-plant wilting with collapsed, brown foliage
- Exposed roots appearing brownish
- Large whitish-tan cankers running along the stem

This points toward a stem canker/vascular wilt disease. My top candidates: Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, Southern_Blight, Verticillium_Wilt, Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot.

Now viewing one reference from each candidate class:

**Analysis of findings:**

- **Test image**: Tomato plant uprooted and laid flat on black surface. Stems show extensive pale/cream-white bleached cankers running longitudinally. Dark discoloration visible within the pale stem sections. Whole plant collapsed with wilted, brown foliage. Exposed root system.

- **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato** (Bugwood_1): Showed marginal leaf scorch/necrosis — leaf symptoms, not the stem cankers seen in the test image. But bacterial canker is also known for elongated, cream-colored stem cankers.

- **Southern_Blight** (Bugwood_2): White mycelium at stem base. Does not match — no mycelium visible in test image.

- **Verticillium_Wilt** (Bugwood_4): Leaf chlorosis and droop, stems externally green. Does not match — test image has prominent external stem bleaching.

- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** (Bugwood_12): Bleached/papery stems on tomato grown on black plastic with branch collapse — very similar plant setting and bleached stem presentation. Strong visual match.

**Decision**: The extensive pale/cream longitudinal bleaching of the stem tissue and the whole-plant collapse most closely match **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**. Sclerotinia causes stems to become bleached, tan, and papery with collapse, exactly as seen. The setting (black plastic mulch) also matches the reference. Bacterial canker typically shows more discrete canker lesions; Sclerotinia bleaches larger stem sections more uniformly.
